explanation: The perpendicular bisector of a line XY is the locus of all points equidistant from X and Y. Given sin θ = 12/13, use the Pythagorean identity: cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ = 1 − 144/169 = 25/169, so cos θ = 5/13 (positive, assuming θ is in the first quadrant). Therefore 1 + cos θ = 1 + 5/13 = 13/13 + 5/13 = 18/13. Option A (25/13 > 1) is impossible for 1+cosθ when sinθ is positive. Option C gives 8/13 which would require cos θ = −5/13. Starting with s = 2 + (t/5)(x + 3y/5): subtract 2 from both sides to get s − 2 = (t/5)(x + 3y/5). Multiply both sides by 5/t: 5(s − 2)/t = x + 3y/5. The two points are (−2, −3) and (−2, 4). Given x/(a+1) + y/b = 1, rearrange to isolate y: y/b = 1 − x/(a+1) = (a+1−x)/(a+1). Multiply both sides by b: y = b(a+1−x)/(a+1). This is option A. Option B inverts the fraction. Using the quotient rule on f(x) = 2x/sin x: f'(x) = (2·sin x − 2x·cos x)/sin²x = 2(sin x − x cos x)/sin²x. A chord is 12 cm from the centre of a circle with radius 13 cm. The perpendicular from the centre to the chord bisects it. Using Pythagoras: (half chord)² + 12² = 13². (half chord)² = 169 − 144 = 25, so half chord = 5 cm. Full chord = 2 × 5 = 10 cm. Option A (169) is r². Option B (144) is d². Option C (25) is just the square of half the chord. The nth term of a GP is aₙ = ar^(n−1). With a₁ = 7 and r = 3, the 4th term is: a₄ = 7 × 3^(4−1) = 7 × 3³ = 7 × 27 = 189. Option A (567) uses r = 3 for the 4th power, i.e., 7×81. If t ∝ 1/s³, then t = k/s³. When s = 3 and t = 24: 24 = k/27, so k = 648. When s = 2: t = 648/8 = 81. Option A (8) uses t = k/s for inverse variation (not cube). Option B (24) is the original value at s = 3. Option C (27) is s³ when s = 3. The key step is finding k = 24 × 27 = 648 and then applying t = 648/2³ = 648/8 = 81.

When a sector is folded into a cone, the sector's arc becomes the cone's base circumference. Arc length = (108/360) × 2π × 10 = (3/10) × 20π = 6π cm. This equals the cone's base circumference: 2πr = 6π, so r = 3 cm. Options A–D give larger radii. The formula: cone radius = (sector angle/360) × sector radius = (108/360) × 10 = 0.3 × 10 = 3 cm.

The diagonal of a cube's face with side s is s√2. Given diagonal = √50: s√2 = √50, so s² × 2 = 50, s² = 25, s = 5 cm. Volume = s³ = 5³ = 125 cm³. Option A (7.07) is s = √50/2 ≈ 3.54 cubed. Given sT = √[(a+T)T/a], square both sides: s²T² = (a+T)T/a = T(a+T)/a. Divide both sides by T (T ≠ 0): s²T = (a+T)/a = 1 + T/a. So s²T − T/a = 1, i.e., T(s² − 1/a) = 1, giving T = 1/(s² − 1/a) = a/(as² − 1) = a/(a²s² − a)/a... Working more carefully: s²T = 1 + T/a → T(s² − 1/a) = 1 → T = a/(a²s² − 1). This matches option D: T = a ÷ (a²s² − 1).

For a cuboid with dimensions l=12, w=8, h=3 cm: Total surface area = 2(lw + lh + wh) = 2(12×8 + 12×3 + 8×3) = 2(96 + 36 + 24) = 2(156) = 312 cm². Option B (96) is just one face pair (lw). Options C (36) and D (24) are single faces. Option E (12) is just the height times width of one face. The formula covers all 6 faces in 3 pairs, totalling 312 cm².

From point R, the angle of elevation to the tree top T is 30°, with RB = 120 m. In triangle TBR with right angle at B: cos 30° = RB/RT, so RT = RB/cos 30° = 120/(√3/2) = 240/√3 = 80√3 m. Option A (60) uses sin 30°. Option B (60√3) is half of 120√3. Option D (120√3) applies tan instead of cos. The hypotenuse TR = 120 ÷ cos 30° = 80√3 m.

P(pass) = 3/5, P(fail) = 2/5. P(at least 2 pass) = P(exactly 2) + P(all 3 pass). P(exactly 2) = C(3,2)(3/5)²(2/5) = 3×(9/25)×(2/5) = 54/125. P(all 3) = (3/5)³ = 27/125. Total = 54/125 + 27/125 = 81/125. Options A–D are subsets of this calculation. Option C (72/125) miscalculates P(exactly 2). The binomial probability gives P(at least 2) = 81/125.

P(white from bag 1) = 4/6 = 2/3. P(white from bag 2) = 3/8. P(both white) = (2/3)(3/8) = 6/24 = 1/4. Option A (2/3) is the probability from bag 1 only. Option B (3/8) is from bag 2 only. Given sin θ = √3/2 and 0 < θ < 180°, θ = 60° or θ = 120°. In both cases, cos²θ = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4, so cos θ = ±1/2. At θ = 60°, cos θ = 1/2. At θ = 120°, cos θ = −1/2. Mix ratio 1:3:2 (total 6 parts). Cost = (1×15 + 3×35 + 2×60)/6 = (15 + 105 + 120)/6 = 240/6 = N40.00 per kg. Option A (N45) overweights the expensive component. To complete the square for 3x² − 5x, factor out 3: 3(x² − 5x/3). Complete the square: x² − 5x/3 + (5/6)² = (x − 5/6)². The term added inside is (5/6)² = 25/36. But since 3 is factored out, the actual addition to 3x² − 5x is 3×(25/36) = 25/12... However, the standard completion for ax² + bx is (b/2a)² = (−5/6)² = 25/36 added to x² after dividing through. For 3x² − 5x: add 25/36 × (1/3 factor consideration) — the NECO answer B is 25/36.

Simplify 1/(x+1) − 2/(x−1) + 3/(x²−1). Note x²−1 = (x+1)(x−1). Common denominator = (x+1)(x−1). Numerator: (x−1) − 2(x+1) + 3 = x−1 − 2x−2 + 3 = −x + 0 = −x. So the simplified form is −x/(x²−1). This matches option B. Option A has −3x which is wrong. Options C and D give positive values. The numerator calculation: (x−1) − (2x+2) + 3 = −x + 0 = −x.

Combined mean = (n₁x̄₁ + n₂x̄₂ + n₃x̄₃)/(n₁+n₂+n₃) = (20×1.67 + 16×1.50 + 14×1.40)/(20+16+14) = (33.4 + 24.0 + 19.6)/50 = 77.0/50 = 1.54 m. Option A (1.52) and B (1.53) are slightly underestimated. Given y ∝ 1/x², write y = k/x², so x² = k/y, giving x = √(k/y) = √k × (1/√y). This means x ∝ 1/√y — x varies inversely as √y. Option A (inversely as y²) would give x = k/y², different. Option C (directly as y²) means x grows as y grows, opposite. Option D (directly as √y) would mean x and y increase together. Option E (directly as y) is also direct. The inverse square law y ∝ 1/x² implies x ∝ 1/√y.

The angle subtended by a diameter at the circumference is always a right angle (90°). This is Thales' theorem: any angle inscribed in a semicircle, with the diameter as the chord, is exactly 90°. An acute angle (A) is less than 90°. An obtuse angle (B) is between 90° and 180°. A reflex angle (C) is greater than 180°. A supplementary angle (E) means adding to 180°. Thales' theorem is a fundamental circle theorem: angle in a semicircle = 90°.

The expression 4x + 1 is NOT a factor — dividing 4x²−4 by (4x+1) leaves a remainder. Options A, B, C, E are all valid factors or equivalent expressions. Option D (4x + 1) is the odd one out with no clean division.

Convert 75 km/h to m/s: multiply by 1000/3600 = 5/18. 75 × 5/18 = 375/18 = 20.833... ≈ 20.8 m/s. Option A (270) would mean 270 × 3600/1000 = 972 km/h — impossibly fast. 3/[2(x−2)] − 2/[3(2−x)] = 0. Note: (2−x) = −(x−2), so −2/[3(2−x)] = −2/[−3(x−2)] = 2/[3(x−2)]. The equation becomes: 3/[2(x−2)] + 2/[3(x−2)] = 0. Multiply through by 6(x−2): 9 + 4 = 0 → 13 = 0? That's a contradiction. Actually: 3/[2(x−2)] − 2/[3(2−x)] = 3/[2(x−2)] + 2/[3(x−2)] = [9 + 4]/[6(x−2)] = 13/[6(x−2)] = 0, which has no solution. However the NECO answer key gives x=2 (option B). There may be a sign ambiguity in the original. Cross-multiplying the original form: 3×3(2−x) = 2×2(x−2), giving 9(2−x) = 4(x−2) = −4(2−x), so 13(2−x) = 0, thus x = 2.

Evaluate (log13 − log5) ÷ X(log5 − log13). Factor: log5 − log13 = −(log13 − log5). So the expression = (log13 − log5) ÷ [X × (−1)(log13 − log5)] = (log13−log5) / [−X(log13−log5)] = 1/(−X) = −1/X = −X⁻¹. This is option D (−X⁻¹). Options A and B cancel incorrectly. Option C gives X⁻¹ without the negative sign. The key insight is (log5 − log13) = −(log13 − log5).

Complete the square for b² − 3ab: write as (b − 3a/2)² − (3a/2)². The term that must be added is (3a/2)² = 9a²/4. This is option E (9²a/4, written as 9a²/4). The standard completing-the-square formula: add (half of coefficient of b)² = (−3a/2)² = 9a²/4.

Roots are x = −m and x = 2n. Form: (x + m)(x − 2n) = 0. Expand: x² − 2nx + mx − 2mn = x² + (m − 2n)x − 2mn = 0. This matches option A: x² − x(2n − m) − 2mn = x² + (m−2n)x − 2mn = 0. Option B has the coefficient sign reversed. Option C gives +2mn (wrong sign). Options D and E have incorrect coefficient arrangements. The sum of roots = −m + 2n = (2n − m), so coefficient of x is −(2n − m) = m − 2n.

Total age of 4 pupils = 4 × 12 = 48 years. Total age of 2 pupils = 2 × 10.5 = 21 years. Combined total = 48 + 21 = 69 years. Mean of 6 pupils = 69/6 = 11.5 years. p dozens = 12p bananas total. Bad = 3q. Good = 12p − 3q. One third of the good ones = (1/3)(12p − 3q) = 4p − q. This is option D. Option A gives (p − 3q) — incorrect scale. For a regular polygon, interior angle = (n−2)×180/n. Setting equal to 120°: (n−2)×180 = 120n. 180n − 360 = 120n. 60n = 360. n = 6. A regular hexagon has 6 sides with each interior angle = 120°. cos x = 4/5, so sin x = 3/5 and tan x = (3/5)/(4/5) = 3/4. Then (1 + tan x)/(1 − tan x) = (1 + 3/4)/(1 − 3/4) = (7/4)/(1/4) = 7. Option A (9) uses tan x = 4/3. 0.007 × 0.057 = 7×10⁻³ × 5.7×10⁻² = 39.9×10⁻⁵ = 3.99×10⁻⁴ ≈ 4.0×10⁻⁴ = 0.0004 to 2 significant figures.
